The chain rule for a multivariable function $f(x,y)$ with two independent variables $s$ and $t,$ where $x=x(s,t)$ and $y=y(s,t),$ can be expressed as follows:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂s}=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s}
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives of $f$ with respect to $x$ and $y:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}=1,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=-1\end{aligned}
$$

Writing the above results in terms of $s$ and $t,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =1, \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we take the derivatives of $x$ and $y$ with respect to $s,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂x}{∂s} & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡t, \\ \frac{∂y}{∂s} & =\operatorname{sin}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting all of our derivatives into the multivariable chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂s} & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\cdot \frac{∂x}{∂s}+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\cdot \frac{∂y}{∂s} \\  & =(1)(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)+(-1)(\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =-(\operatorname{cos}⁡t+\operatorname{sin}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The gradient of the function $f(x,y,z)$ is defined as

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\,k.
$$

Since $∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z),$ the function $f(x,y,z)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=4xy,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2{x}^{2}+2yz,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}={y}^{2}+1
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y$ and $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =\int \frac{∂f}{∂x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int 4xy\,\text{d}x \\  & =2{x}^{2}y+g(y,z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2{x}^{2}+\frac{∂g}{∂y}
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=2{x}^{2}+2yz$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}+\frac{∂g}{∂y} & =2{x}^{2}+2yz \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =2yz\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate $\frac{∂g}{∂y}$ with respect to $y.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(y,z) & =\int \frac{∂g}{∂y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\int 2yz\,\text{d}y \\  & ={y}^{2}z+h(z)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $g(y,z)={y}^{2}z+h(z)$ in the expression for $f(x,y,z),$ we get

$$
f(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}z+h(z).
$$

To determine the function $h(z),$ we differentiate $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z.$ This gives

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂z}={y}^{2}+{h}^{′}(z).
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂z}={y}^{2}+1$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}+1 & ={y}^{2}+{h}^{′}(z) \\ {h}^{′}(z) & =1 \\ h(z) & =z+C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Consequently,

$$
f(x,y,z)=2{x}^{2}y+{y}^{2}z+z+C.
$$

$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14182795/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1\},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=2v(1-u-v),\,y=\frac{1-v}{1+u}.
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{4}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{4}.$

For the side ${S}_{4},$ we have $u=0$ and $1\ge v\ge 0.$ Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(2v(1-u-v),\,\frac{1-v}{1+u}) \\  & =(2v(1-0-v),\,\frac{1-v}{1+0}) \\  & =(2v(1-v),\,1-v).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{4}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=2v(1-v),\,y=1-v,\,1\ge v\ge 0.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x=2t(1-t),\,y=1-t,\,1\ge t\ge 0.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
x=2(1-y)(y)\,⇒\,x=-2{(y-\frac{1}{2})}^{2}+\frac{1}{2}
$$

which is a left-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(\frac{1}{2},\frac{1}{2}).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{4}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(0,1)\to (2(1)(1-0-1),\frac{1-1}{1+0})=(0,0) \\  & T:(0,0)\to (2(0)(1-0-0),\frac{1-0}{1+0})=(0,1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{4}$ is an arc of a left-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(0,1).$

questions.problem:
Find the coordinates of the vector $x$ relative to the basis $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2},{b}_{3}\},$ where

$$
{b}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{b}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,x=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}].
$$

If $[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]$ then what is the value of ${x}_{2}?$
questions.worked_solution:
Remember, the order of the vectors in a basis is important.

Notice that 

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{x}={{(\,2\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{1}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{1}}+{{(\,3\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{2}}+{{(\,6\,)}_{⏟}}_{{x}_{3}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{b}_{3}}
$$

which means that

$$
x=2\cdot {b}_{1}+3\cdot {b}_{2}+6\cdot {b}_{3}
$$

and therefore 

$$
[x]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 6\end{aligned}],
$$

Finally, ${x}_{2}=3.$

questions.problem: Suppose $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and $det(A)=6.$ The matrix $B$ is obtained from $A$ by applying the elementary row operations ${R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}$ and ${R}_{3}:=4{R}_{3}.$ What is the value of $det(B)?$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's figure out what each operation does to the determinant.

- The operation ${R}_{2}↔{R}_{3}$ involves swapping two rows, so it changes the sign of the determinant to the opposite one.

- The operation ${R}_{3}:=4{R}_{3}$ involves multiplying a row by $4,$ so the determinant is multiplied by $4$ as well.

Therefore, we have to change the sign of the determinant to the opposite one and multiply by $4$ as well. Consequently, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =4\cdot (-det(A)) \\  & =-4det(A) \\  & =-4\cdot 6 \\  & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$
